Worked example: Harvest Lane's order router, HL · Route orders.

Switch (Mode: Rules), with the fallback output turned on in Options:

  • 0 · Number: {{ Number($json.total) }} is greater than or equal to 100000 → Edit Fields: route = "Bulk: call to confirm"
  • 1 · String: {{ $json.type }} equals subscription → route = "Weekly box list"
  • 2 · String: type equals pickup → route = "Pickup slip"
  • 3 · String: type equals delivery → route = "Rider list"
  • 4 · Fallback → route = "Check: unknown type" (later, an email to Tolu)

HL-0101subscription₦18,0001 · Weekly box

HL-0103pickup₦6,5002 · Pickup slip
HL-0104pickup₦9,0002 · Pickup slip
HL-0105delivery₦34,0003 · Rider list

Evidence: a screenshot of the executed Switch showing the item count on each output (output 0: 1, output 1: 2, output 2: 2, output 3: 2, output 4: 1), with "Send data to all matching outputs" left off so the ₦150,000 delivery appears only on Bulk.
mistakes: Forgetting to turn on the fallback output, so the "collection" order goes nowhere without an error.
Putting the Bulk rule last, so the ₦150,000 delivery lands on the Rider list.
Comparing total as a string, so 150000 vs 100000 is judged as text or throws a wrong-type error.
Turning on "send to all matching outputs", so the bulk delivery appears on two routes.
b.pass: An executed Switch with five outputs where the eight pinned orders split 2/2/2/1/1, the ₦150,000 delivery appears only on Bulk, and "collection" appears on the fallback.
b.redo: Send it back if any order is missing or appears twice, or there is no fallback output.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane test data. Input 1 is Orders, Input 2 is Customers, matched on customer_id on both sides.

  • Orders: HL-0071 (C-014), HL-0072 (C-022), HL-0073 (C-009), HL-0077 (C-099, no such customer)
  • Customers: C-014 Mrs Adebayo, C-022 Mr Okafor, C-009 Iya Basira, C-031 Chef Tunde (no orders this week)
Merge settingPredicted itemsWhat comes outHarvest Lane use
Keep matches3HL-0071, 0072, 0073, each with the customer's name, phone and area added. HL-0077 and Chef Tunde are gone.Delivery messages: only orders you can actually address.
Enrich Input 14All four orders; HL-0077 has no name or phone fields. Chef Tunde is not included.The Outbox, where no order may vanish: an IF on "name is empty" flags HL-0077 for Tolu.
Keep non-matches, output from Input 11HL-0077 only.An "orphan orders" check: orders typed with a wrong customer ID.
Keep non-matches, both inputs2HL-0077 and C-031 Chef Tunde.One clean-up list: bad orders plus customers who didn't order (a win-back list, if they've agreed to hear from you).

How to predict: write the four IDs from each side in two columns, draw a line between equal customer_ids, then read the mode: matches are the lines, non-matches are the loose ends, enrich keeps every Input 1 row with or without a line.

Log: predicted and actual count for each run, a screenshot of each Merge output, and one sentence per mode naming its use. If a count surprises you, check that both sides really use customer_id with the same spelling and type (C-014 as text on both sides).
mistakes: Running the modes without writing a prediction first, so the log shows results but not understanding.
Forgetting the orphan order or the order-less customer, so all modes give the same count.
Matching on name instead of customer_id.
Mixing up which input is Input 1, so enrich keeps customers instead of orders.
s.pass: For each of the three modes the log shows a predicted count, the actual count and the records that appear (matching the test data), plus a named Harvest Lane use for each.
s.redo: Send it back if predictions are missing, counts don't follow from the data, or the orphan order and lonely customer weren't included.

g.answer:
Worked example (fictional): Lantern Hill School, Abeokuta, sends a PTA meeting reminder to 60 parents. All names and numbers are made up, and Send writes to a Sent log rather than messaging anyone.

Build: Manual Trigger → Contacts (60 rows) and Do not contact (5 rows) → Merge, matching fields contact_id, keep non-matches, output from Input 1 → IF phone is not empty (false → Fix list) → Loop Over Items (batch 20) → Build message → Send (log) with sent_at = {{ $now.toFormat('HH:mm:ss') }} → Wait 60 s → back into the loop. Done → Gmail to the head teacher, Execute Once on, "Reminders sent: {{ $input.all().length }}".

Pace: the provider's published limit, as written in the learner's log with the page it came from, was 30 messages a minute. Batches of 20 with 60-second waits never exceed 20 a minute.

CheckResult
Contacts in60
Removed by Merge (do not contact)5, none in Sent log
Fix list (no phone)4
Sent log rows51
Batch 1 sent_at09:00:02 to 09:00:05 (20 rows)
Batch 2 sent_at09:01:06 to 09:01:09 (20 rows)
Batch 3 sent_at09:02:10 to 09:02:12 (11 rows)
Summary emails1 ("Reminders sent: 51")

Sum check: 51 + 5 + 4 = 60, so no contact disappeared.

Submit: the canvas screenshot, the Sent log with the three clusters visible (phones masked), the Fix list, the single summary email, and your batch-planner numbers with the limit's source.
mistakes: Sending real messages to real people from a practice build instead of writing to a Sent log.
Leaving the Wait on the done branch or not wiring the last node back into the loop.
Getting several summary emails because Execute Once was left off.
Picking a batch size and wait without a source for the provider's limit, or sharing unmasked contact screenshots.
g.pass: The Sent log shows timestamp clusters spaced by the planned wait, sent + excluded + Fix list equals the input count, no do-not-contact entry appears, exactly one summary arrives, and the limit's source is noted.
g.redo: Send it back if batches aren't visibly spaced, counts don't add up, an excluded contact was sent to, or personal data is shown unmasked.
